source_documents.title: Playing with substitution in N-methyl pyridinium phenol superphotoacids to tune the interplay between intramolecular charge transfer and excited-state proton transfer

reference_evidence_units.quote: ESPT was found to be operative for all the investigated ortho isomers on a picosecond time scale, as revealed by ultrafast transient absorption spectroscopy, in both water (where pKa* < 0) and alcoholic solvents.
reference_evidence_units.subject: ortho isomers 2-5
reference_evidence_units.statement: Picosecond excited-state proton transfer (to solvent) in all ortho isomers.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Proton transfer is to the solvent, not intramolecular.

reference_evidence_units.quote: ICT from the phenolic ring to the N-methylpyridinium moiety is responsible for the photoacid behaviour and is enhanced by the pos itive mesomeric effect of the substituent
reference_evidence_units.subject: series 1-5
reference_evidence_units.statement: Intramolecular charge transfer drives the photoacidity.

reference_evidence_units.quote: However, they undergo charge transfer in the relaxed excited state, so that they are typically weak emitters.
reference_evidence_units.subject: series 1-5
reference_evidence_units.statement: A dipolar relaxed CT state makes most of them weak emitters.

reference_mechanisms.label: ICT_TICT_CT
reference_mechanisms.rationale: ICT governs photoacidity and the weak emission of the relaxed CT state.

reference_mechanisms.rationale: Excited-state proton transfer (to solvent) measured by fsTA; the family covers proton-transfer photophysics.
